popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Homer's Bellerophon digression (Iliad 6) makes Glaucus of Ephyra — Sisyphus' son — the father who passes the Corinthian line to the Chimera-slayer.

popCulture.title: Glaucus (son of Sisyphus)
popCulture.description: King of Corinth (Ephyra); father of Bellerophon. Later myth also feeds him to his own mares at Potniae — a grim death distinct from Glaucus of Lycia.

popCulture.title: Bibliotheca
popCulture.creator: Pseudo-Apollodorus
popCulture.description: Apollodorus keeps Glaucus in the Sisyphid stem and the Potniae horses among the Corinthian king's fatal stories.
